name: Floral bouquet fragrances

card.summary: Perfumes that blend several flower scents into one composition, used to give a polished, fragrant impression.
card.note: Fragrance ingredients can irritate sensitive skin.

quick.overview:
A floral bouquet fragrance blends the scents of several flowers rather than centring on one. Wikipedia's perfume article lists Houbigant's Quelques Fleurs and Jean Patou's Joy as examples.

In looksmaxxing and style discussions, scent is part of overall presentation: wearing a pleasant fragrance adds to how someone is perceived alongside grooming and clothing. No studies of floral bouquet scents specifically were found.
quick.how: Wearers apply the fragrance to skin or clothing as they would other perfumes, choosing among soliflore, bouquet or bright floral styles for the impression they want.
quick.risks: Fragrance can cause skin irritation or allergy in some people; trying a small amount first is common practice.

lead: Floral bouquet fragrances are perfumes that combine several flower scents into one blend. They sit alongside the single-flower soliflore style, such as Serge Lutens' Sa Majeste La Rose, and the modern bright floral style that merges both, such as Estee Lauder's Beautiful [1].

In Michael Edwards's fragrance wheel, floral is a main family with subfamilies Floral, Soft Floral and Floral Amber [2]. Flower cultivation for perfume essences began in the 14th century and grew into a major industry in southern France [1].

chain: Added to overall grooming and presence
angle.text: Fragrance adds to personal presentation alongside grooming. A bouquet blend is one of the classic styles people choose.

paras: The bouquet style is one of the floral categories described for perfume: single floral, floral bouquet and bright floral [1].
Edwards's wheel, revised in 2008, classes Floral as one of its main families next to Woody, Amber and Fresh; Chanel No. 5 is placed in the Soft Floral subfamily [2].
